initial.name: 01-line-equipment.png
initial.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Redesign the supplied real FactoryLM Hub screenshot as a professional tablet interface for a maintenance technician at a large factory with several production lines and thousands of components per line. Create ONE full-frame landscape app screenshot, 8:5 aspect, 2304x1440 if possible. No device bezel, browser/OS chrome, perspective or presentation-board framing.
MANDATORY FactoryLM style guide: flat solid backgrounds only; NO gradients, glow, glass, bevels, heavy shadows, decorative illustrations, sparkle/AI icons, emoji, huge hero headings, repeated call-to-action cards, oversized pills or bento cards. Compact but comfortable information density: large enough 44px touch rows, readable 15px-equivalent body text, modest 22px-equivalent page title. Use rectangular table/list rows separated by thin rules; 6px corners only on controls. White #ffffff surfaces on #f3f4f6 background; navy #111827 slim header; text #1f2937, secondary #6b7280; rules #e5e7eb; ONE indigo #4f46e5 accent, only for selected items and the single main action. Status colors only when meaningful, with text. Monospaced equipment tags. No decorative colored status dots or invented running/healthy claims.
FactoryLM wordmark top-left, header site selector "North Plant ▾"; compact navigation "Equipment", "Conversations", "Projects", with Equipment active. Header-wide search and its explicit scope. No marketing copy, greetings, AI jargon, readiness scores or fake urgency.
All plant names, machines and counts are illustrative data. Footer on every image, exactly "Design proposal · Example plant data". Keep all labels crisp and correctly spelled. Scope, location and physical identity matter more than branding.

SCREEN 1 — LINE EQUIPMENT, NOT A CARD DASHBOARD.
Top search "Find tag, machine or part number" and scope dropdown "In North Plant". Left navigation pane width about 250px: heading "Browse"; expanded "North Plant", expanded "Packaging", then "Line 01", "Line 02", "Line 03" selected with indigo left rule, "Line 04"; collapsed "Processing", collapsed "Utilities". Below a thin divider heading "Recent" with two simple links "CV-301 / MLC" and "PK-304 / VFD1". Do not expand thousands of components in the sidebar.
Main content breadcrumb "North Plant / Packaging / Line 03". Modest title "Line 03", supporting count "50 machines · 2,500 components". Counts are plain text, NOT KPI cards. Toolbar "Machines" selected and "Components" as two quiet tabs; search field "Filter machines on Line 03". Main full-width machine table columns "Tag", "Machine", "Location", "Components". Exactly six visible example rows:
CV-301 | Infeed conveyor | Station 01 | 50
CV-302 | Transfer conveyor | Station 02 | 50
PK-303 | Case packer | Station 03 | 50
PK-304 | Cartoner | Station 04 | 50
CV-305 | Discharge conveyor | Station 05 | 50
PL-306 | Palletizer | Station 06 | 50
Clickable tags and quiet trailing chevrons, no separate Open button repeated on every row. Footer beneath table "Showing 1–6 of 50 machines" and simple Previous / Next pagination. Machine rows compact with 56px-equivalent height. Leave moderate usable space, not enormous padding. No line health claims; do not show a thousand cards. The hierarchy is available but search is always accessible.

SCREEN 2 — FIND THE RIGHT INSTANCE WHEN TAGS REPEAT.
Header search contains "MLC" with explicit scope "In North Plant", clear X. Left browse pane matches screen 1: North Plant > Packaging > Lines 01, 02, 03, 04, then collapsed Processing and Utilities. Main title "Results for MLC", supporting "400 components in North Plant". Compact filter controls "Area: All", "Line: All", "Type: All". A simple full-width list, not cards, with columns "Tag", "Component", "Machine", "Location". Exactly six rows:
MLC | Main contactor | CV-101 · Infeed conveyor | Packaging / Line 01 / Station 01
MLC | Main contactor | CV-201 · Infeed conveyor | Packaging / Line 02 / Station 01
MLC | Label not checked | CV-301 · Infeed conveyor | Packaging / Line 03 / Station 01
MLC | Main contactor | CV-302 · Transfer conveyor | Packaging / Line 03 / Station 02
MLC | Main contactor | PK-303 · Case packer | Packaging / Line 03 / Station 03
MLC | Main contactor | CV-401 · Infeed conveyor | Packaging / Line 04 / Station 01
Highlight ONLY CV-301's row with solid pale indigo #eef2ff and a thin left indigo rule. Mark its Tag "MLC" in monospace. Each row has its own complete location visible, even though the tags and equipment names repeat.
Under table "Showing 1–6 of 400 components" and Previous / Next. Small plain instruction beside selected result "Open CV-301 / MLC" as the single primary action. Never auto-select a result solely because the tag or part number matches. No green identity badges. This screen must show why exact physical context matters at scale.

SCREEN 3 — ONE MACHINE WITH MANY COMPONENTS.
Same North Plant site header and compact browser navigation. Breadcrumb "North Plant / Packaging / Line 03 / CV-301". Main title "CV-301 · Infeed conveyor"; secondary "Station 01". Plain navigation tabs "Components" selected, "Manuals", "Work history", "Conversation". One compact "Ask about CV-301" button in the title toolbar, no duplicated actions.
Content "50 components", search "Find a tag or component on CV-301", filter "Assembly: All". Table columns "Tag", "Component", "Assembly", "Physical location". Eight rows:
VFD1 | Drive | Infeed | CP-01 · Row 2
M1 | Motor | Infeed | Under belt
MLC | Label not checked | Main power | CP-01 · Row 1
PS1 | 24 V supply | Main power | CP-01 · Row 1
PE1 | Photoeye | Infeed | Entry guide
PE2 | Photoeye | Infeed | Exit guide
ES1 | Emergency stop | Operator station | Left side
PB1 | Start button | Operator station | Left side
Highlight the MLC row subtly, with small amber warning glyph beside "Label not checked" but dark readable text. Use real containment/function group concepts without inventing a dependency tree: VFD1 and M1 are sibling rows, never motor under drive. Cabinet location is a COLUMN, not a forced duplicate hierarchy.
Below table "Showing 1–8 of 50 components" and Previous / Next. Bottom concise selected-component action "Open MLC", no inventory-completion scores. The right result is distinguished by machine + component tag + physical location. No operational statuses or catalog numbers invented.

SCREEN 4 — COMPONENT WORKSPACE WITH PRECISE LOCATION.
Site header North Plant with global search "Find tag, machine or part number". No deep sidebar tree on this focused screen: narrow left rail with Equipment, Conversations, Projects and a "Back to CV-301" link. Content breadcrumb "North Plant / Packaging / Line 03 / CV-301 / MLC". Title "MLC"; secondary "CV-301 · Infeed conveyor · Station 01"; second compact line "Physical location: CP-01 · Row 1". Small amber indicator with dark text "Label not checked" and an outlined "Check label" action.
Simple tabs "Conversation" selected, "Manuals", "Work history", "Connections". Main area is conversation on left, source/reference on right. User asks "What is the coil voltage on this MLC?" Plain MIRA response with NO sparkle icon: "Check the component label first. This document alone does not identify the installed MLC." A quiet "Check label" link follows, not another large card.
Right pane titled "Reference document" with "CA3KN22BD-maker.pdf", "Page 1". Small plain two-column data rows "Catalog number   CA3KN22BD", "Control voltage   24 V DC", "Contacts   2 NO + 2 NC". Below in dark readable text "Catalog data. Match to installed MLC not checked." Action "Open source page". NO implication this is installed state or real wiring.
Composer anchored at bottom of conversation column. Directly above it, a permanent compact two-line context strip:
"About: Line 03 / CV-301 / MLC" and "North Plant / Packaging", with "Change" link.
Text input "Ask about MLC…" with attach icon and ONE filled indigo Send button. Context strip and source must not overlap chat. Long ancestors are in breadcrumb, the minimum disambiguating machine + component remain in view. No generic assistant welcome, purple message backgrounds, redundant cards, glossy effects or giant whitespace.
